notes:
63 of the 65 stations have a row. Two get null, and both are observer stations rather than lights: Fair Isle (Findlay 1887 has no Fair Isle light) and Hynish Signal Tower (the shore station for Skerryvore).

Things to check:
1. North Carr L.V. (p63r25): Findlay gives it only as 'Lightvessel proposed with fixed bright light' (1887), yet the reports print 'Carr Rock Light-ship' from 1885. The position is fine to use, but the character may not be what the vessel actually showed. Look in a later Findlay edition or the Northern Lighthouse Board records for when it was placed. If 'proposed' counts as 'not yet placed' for you, make this one null.
2. Shared rows: Hoy Low and Hoy High both get p65r23 (high light is item 1, low light item 2). Several single stations have two lights in one row: Pentland Skerries, Girdle Ness, Isle of May (high and low), Pladda, and Stornoway/Arnish (item 1 is the Arnish tower). Nowhere in this table does Findlay print a station's lights in separate rows, so every extra_rows list is empty.
3. Opening dates: Findlay dates Ailsa Craig 1886, but the reports list it from 1885. Fidra (1885) fits. The 1885 entries may be the stations' first year rather than a mismatch.
4. Name traps, all settled by position and coast order: Start Point is the Orkney light (on Sanday, 59 16.6 N). Sanda is the island off Kintyre. Findlay's 'Oronsay Island' is Isle Ornsay in Sleat Sound, not Oronsay by Colonsay. MONTROSE NESS (Scurdy Ness, p64r5) is not Montrose Harbour (p64r6). Corran Point is filed under 'Loch Eil'. Skervuile is 'Sgeir Maoile or Iron Rock'.
5. Findlay's p66 runs the Northern Isles from south to north (Start Point, then North Ronaldsha up to North Unst), the reverse of the reports' order. The rows match by name and position, so this doesn't affect the matches.
